title: Crew-Plan Contract
description: Machine-checkable form of an outcome orchestrator's PLAN-pass return value. Grounded verbatim in conductor/orchestra-model.md §3.1 ('Required shape') and §3.2 ('Rules the plan must satisfy — the conductor rejects a plan that violates these'). `tasks[].brief` $refs brief.schema.json directly: §3.2 rule 1 states the crew-plan 'is a carrier of dispatch briefs, not a replacement for them' — every task brief is the VERBATIM six-field contract, not a paraphrase. Phase 0 / Design Decision #3.

mission_id.description: Ties to the mission-states.md FSM record. HIGH-3 FIX (Fable adversarial review, BLOCK finding — 'task.id path traversal -> write OUTSIDE the repo'): constrained to a safe slug — lowercase alnum first character, then alnum/'.'/'_'/'-' only. No '/' (or '\') can ever appear, so no path-traversal payload validates. `tessctl run` builds `missions/<mission_id>/...` directly from this field (`_run_artifact_path`, `_mission_dir` in the RUN region of `.tess/bin/tessctl`) with no other sanitization step, so it needs the identical path-traversal-proof constraint Task.id gets below. `tessctl mission new` already only ever produces safe, date-prefixed slugs via its own `_slugify()` helper — this pins that same safety guarantee at the crew-plan contract boundary too, for a hand-authored or orchestrator-produced plan file that never went through `mission new`. (Note: `mission.schema.json`'s own primary-key field, named `id` there, is a separate field this PR does not touch — see `.tess/bin/tessctl`'s RUN region for the belt-and-suspenders runtime containment check that covers this class of id regardless of which contract produced it.)

outcome_owner.description: §3.2 rule 6 — 'One outcome owner. Exactly one outcome_owner; no co-owners.' Modeled as a single string, not an array, so co-ownership is structurally impossible rather than merely discouraged.

notes.description: §3.1 — framing the conductor needs before dispatch.

stages.description: §3.1 — ordered; stage N+1 starts only when stage N's gate clears (enforced by the conductor loop §4a, not by this schema).

owner.description: §3.1 — orchestrator name, or 'tess' for lighter missions.

inputs.description: Task ids whose artifacts feed synthesis. tessctl validate additionally lints that every entry matches a real task id in stages[] (business rule beyond plain JSON Schema).

escalations.description: §3.1 — conditions that bounce the whole mission back to Tess/the operator.

gate_in.description: §3.2 rule 3 — 'gate_in references a real gate from doctrine.md.' These five are the canonical dependency-gate names per doctrine.md's own CHANGELOG and orchestra-model.md §3.2 rule 3. M5 (Fable adversarial review): the §3.3 worked example previously used the shorthand literal 'intake-complete' for this same gate instead of the canonical 'intake-before-anything' and a prose `milestones` string instead of the schema's array-of-{deliverable,acceptance_evidence,owner} shape; both were reconciled directly in orchestra-model.md §3.3 in this Phase 0 PR so the doctrine text now matches what this schema actually enforces.

parallel.description: §3.1/§3.2 rule 7 — 'Parallelism is explicit. parallel:true asserts the tasks share no state and have no intra-stage depends_on edges.' The no-intra-stage-edges half of this rule is enforced as a lint check by tessctl validate (a relational, cross-array-item constraint plain JSON Schema cannot express), not by this schema block alone.

id.description: HIGH-3 FIX (Fable adversarial review, BLOCK finding, reproduced: `id: "../../../../../../tmp/PWNED"` validated PASS and wrote OUTSIDE root, escaping `never_touch`). A safe slug only — lowercase alnum first character, then alnum/'.'/'_'/'-'. No '/' (or '\') is permitted at all, so no path-traversal payload can ever validate: `_run_artifact_path` in the RUN region of `.tess/bin/tessctl` builds `missions/<mission_id>/returns/<task_id>.<ext>` directly from this field, with the dispatched task's own process (not just the conductor's own file operations) writing to that exact contracted path.

agent.description: §3.2 rule 2 — must be a real, dispatchable agent definition, or 'general-purpose' paired with flag_for_tess. Cross-checking against the installed roster (.claude/agents/*) is left to a Phase 1 lint extension — this schema checks shape, not roster membership.

role.description: §6 — every task carries a role so two players never collide on the same responsibility.

brief.description: §3.2 rule 1 — the full six-field Dispatch Brief Contract, VERBATIM REQUIRED.

flag_for_tess.description: §3.2 rule 2 — set when 'agent' is 'general-purpose' because the needed specialist does not yet exist; names the capability gap so it is logged, never silently skipped.

then.$comment: §3.2 rule 4: 'verifier.required: true for any task that is prod-touching, client-facing, externally-visible, or informs an irreversible decision.' prod_touching/client_facing/externally_visible/irreversible_decision are Phase-0 machine-checkable proxies for those prose criteria, mirroring brief.schema.json's prod_touching/estimated_minutes proxies. H1 FIX (Fable adversarial review, BLOCK finding): the original version of this branch only forced `verifier.required: true`, which the base `Verifier` $defs (necessarily, for the legitimate null-verifier case) allows to coexist with `agent: null` and `primary_artifacts: []` — so a task marked prod_touching/client_facing/externally_visible/irreversible_decision could carry `verifier: {agent: null, required: true, primary_artifacts: []}` and PASS: a null-verifier bypass on exactly the class of task verification-routing.md says must never skip mandatory review. This branch now ALSO re-pins `agent` to one of the six named mandatory verifiers (the `enum` excludes `null`, which the base Verifier schema permits only for the true internal-only/not-irreversible case) and requires `primary_artifacts` to carry at least one real artifact — closing the bypass without changing the shape for legitimately-internal, non-triggering tasks (where this `then` branch never fires).

agent.description: verification-routing.md's six named mandatory verifiers. §3.1: 'null only if internal-only AND not irreversible.'

primary_artifacts.description: The real outputs the verifier must read itself — never a summary (verification-routing.md 'Verifier Brief Standard').

$comment: Minimal-validator keyword subset supported by tessctl validate: type, enum, const, properties, required, additionalProperties, items, minItems, maxItems, minLength, maxLength, pattern, minimum, maximum, exclusiveMinimum, exclusiveMaximum, if/then/else, oneOf, anyOf, allOf, contains, $ref, $defs.
